summary: High p95 latency and 504s across reserved GPU reservation after tenant mix change — suspected GPU affinity and autoscaler sizing gap
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reported a sustained p95 latency increase and a rising number of 504 gateway errors across their dedicated GPU reservation during evening traffic (18:00–20:00 PDT). The spike began after a tenant mix change when a new high-concurrency tenant was onboarded into the same reservation. Initial hypothesis points to GPU affinity/misalignment combined with autoscaler target sizing that did not account for the new job mix.

Impact:
- Multiple BrightCart endpoints experienced p95 latency increase from ~120ms to 900–1,200ms and an elevated rate of 504s (~2% of requests) for ~90 minutes.
- Customer reports degraded user experience in production peak window; marketing campaign affected.

Timeline (local times):
- 2026-03-10 17:45 PDT: BrightCart opened a support chat reporting slow responses.
- 2026-03-10 17:58 PDT: Support created ticket SUP-274983.
- 2026-03-10 18:05 PDT: Observability shows p95 trending upward; spike correlated with new tenant traffic ingestion.
- 2026-03-10 18:20 PDT: Mitigation: routing fallback to smaller model variant for high-latency routes.
- 2026-03-10 18:45 PDT: Ops increased autoscale target for the reservation as an interim measure.

Environment:
- Dedicated reservation: resv-cc-84 (us-west-2)
- Node types: A100-sliced and V100-legacy mix
- Serving runtime: 3.14.1
- Autoscaler policy: conservative target (min:4, desired:6, max:12) with scale cooldown 300s

Steps to reproduce (observed reproducible pattern):
1) Run mixed traffic with a small number of long-sequence streaming requests concurrently with a burst of short-chat requests from a second tenant.
2) Observe GPU allocation and affinity mapping via /debug/affinity endpoint.
3) Watch queue length and per-GPU microbatching metrics.

Observed behavior:
- GPUs servicing the long-seq tenant saturated VRAM and started preempting KV caches, leading to increased microbatch latency and head-of-line blocking.
- Scheduler placed new short-chat pods onto already hot GPUs due to affinity scoring not penalizing per-sequence memory usage.
- Autoscaler did not scale quickly enough because observed throughput deltas were smoothed by the averaging window.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Shifted BrightCart heavier routes to fallback model variant (gptx-2.7b-16k-quant-lite) for low-latency paths.
- Increased desired autoscale target from 6 to 9 for resv-cc-84.
- Isolated the high-concurrency tenant onto a separate reservation as a stopgap.

Next steps planned:
- Short term: Tune affinity scoring to consider per-sequence VRAM footprint and adapt scheduler penalties.
- Short-to-mid term: Adjust autoscaler sensitivity (shorter smoothing window during peak hours) and lower cooldown for dedicated pools.
- Postmortem: Run capacity planning for mixed job mixes and update onboarding checklist for new tenants into reservations.

investigation_notes: Affinity scoring: discovered it ignores per-request sequence length and KV-cache pressure; low penalty allowed colocating heavy long-seq and bursty short requests.
Autoscaler: configured with a 5-minute smoothing window and 300s cooldown; with mixed workloads the instantaneous need was masked and scaling lagged during the spike.
Serving runtime: KV cache thrashing observed on GPUs with >80% VRAM, causing serialization of microbatches and p95 degradation.
Hypothesis: Combination of scheduler affinity mismatch + autoscale smoothing window caused sustained tail latency, not a single GPU hardware fault.
resolution: Mitigations applied: isolated noisy tenant and increased desired autoscale target to 9; routed latency-sensitive endpoints to lighter model variant. Engineering tasks opened to: 1) update affinity scoring to include estimated KV VRAM per-request (PR linked), 2) reduce autoscaler smoothing window during peak hours and lower cooldown for dedicated reservations, 3) add automated onboarding checks to flag high-KV workloads before co-locating. Long-term: capacity planning and reservation placement policy update. Ticket remains In Progress until affinity change is deployed and observed over two peak cycles.
